title: Family Life in Istanbul: Raising children with confidence
excerpt: Moving to Istanbul with children brings a new set of questions. How do you choose a school? What’s the difference between a kreş and an anaokulu? The good news is that thousands of Turkish and international families successfully raise children in Istanbul. The city offers excellent healthcare, a wide choice of schools, plenty of parks, and countless family-friendly activities. This guide explains what you need to know to help your family settle into everyday life.
bodyHtml:
Childcare and Preschool

For younger children, Istanbul offers several childcare options.

These include:

  • Private day-care centres (Kreş)

  • Public and private preschools (Anaokulu)

  • Montessori schools

  • International preschools

  • Nursery schools

The minimum admission age varies between schools, with many accepting children from around two or three years old.

Popular schools often have waiting lists, so it’s advisable to begin your search several months before you need a place.

Schools

Families can choose from several education systems.

Public Schools

Public schools are free for children who meet the enrolment requirements and primarily teach in Turkish.

Private Turkish Schools

Private schools generally offer:

  • Smaller class sizes

  • Additional foreign language education

  • Modern facilities

  • Extracurricular activities

Tuition fees vary considerably.

International Schools

Istanbul has a wide range of international schools offering:

  • British curriculum

  • American curriculum

  • International Baccalaureate (IB)

  • French curriculum

  • German curriculum

  • Italian curriculum

  • Other national programmes

Admission requirements, tuition fees, and waiting lists vary by school.

University Education

Istanbul is home to many well-regarded public and private universities.

Several institutions offer undergraduate and postgraduate programmes taught entirely in English.

Healthcare for Children

Children have access to both public and private healthcare throughout Istanbul.

Families can choose between:

  • Family Health Centres (Aile Sağlığı Merkezi)

  • Public hospitals

  • Private hospitals

  • Specialist children’s hospitals

Many private hospitals have English-speaking paediatricians and international patient departments.

If you have SGK or private health insurance, check which hospitals and clinics are covered by your policy before making an appointment.

Vaccinations

Türkiye operates a national childhood immunisation programme through the public healthcare system.

Routine childhood vaccinations are also available through many private hospitals and clinics.

If you’re moving from another country, bring your child’s vaccination records so your doctor can determine whether any additional vaccines or schedule adjustments are needed.

Emergency Care

For medical emergencies, call 112.

Emergency departments operate 24 hours a day.

For non-life-threatening illnesses, many families choose private hospitals because waiting times are often shorter.

Parks and Outdoor Spaces

Although Istanbul is a busy metropolitan city, it has plenty of green spaces for families.

You’ll find:

  • Children’s playgrounds

  • Neighbourhood parks

  • Waterfront promenades

  • Forest parks

  • Picnic areas

  • Beaches during the summer season

Most residential neighbourhoods have at least one public playground nearby.

Family Activities

There are activities for children throughout the year.

Popular options include:

  • Bosphorus ferry rides

  • The Princes’ Islands

  • Aquariums

  • Museums

  • Science centres

  • Theme parks

  • Indoor play centres

  • Nature parks

Many museums and cultural attractions offer discounted admission for children.

Public Transport with Children

An İstanbulkart is the easiest way to travel as a family.

Most metro and Marmaray stations provide:

  • Lifts or escalators

  • Space for pushchairs

  • Step-free access where available

Children under seven travel free on Istanbul’s public transport when accompanied by an adult.

Shopping for Children

Most shopping centres include:

  • Baby changing rooms

  • Family toilets

  • Children’s play areas

  • Nursing rooms

Baby products, clothing, and children’s equipment are widely available through supermarkets, pharmacies, shopping malls, and specialist baby stores.

Safety

Istanbul is generally considered a safe city for families.

As with any major city:

  • Supervise children in busy public places.

  • Hold young children’s hands near roads and public transport.

  • Teach children basic road safety.

  • Keep emergency contact numbers readily available.

When choosing where to live, visit the neighbourhood at different times of the day to get a better sense of the local environment.

Pets and Children

Istanbul is famous for its community cats.

Most are accustomed to people and are cared for by local residents, but children should always avoid touching unfamiliar animals without adult supervision.

Veterinary clinics are widely available throughout the city.

Finding Other Families

Building a support network makes settling into Istanbul much easier.

Many families meet through:

  • School communities

  • Parent groups

  • Sports clubs

  • Children’s activities

  • Community organisations

  • Local neighbourhood events

Making friends often helps children settle just as quickly as adults.

The Little Things

Children usually adapt faster than their parents.

Before long, they’ll know which playground they love, which bakery sells their favourite pastry, and which ferry ride is the most exciting.

Meanwhile, parents are still learning how to pay utility bills, book doctor’s appointments, and navigate the school system.

That’s completely normal.

Every family settles at its own pace.

Final Tip

No one arrives in Istanbul knowing exactly how everything works.

Take your time, ask questions, and connect with other families who have already been through the same experience.

If you’re looking to meet local and international families, Smileys Community regularly organises family-friendly picnics, sailing trips, outdoor activities, seasonal events, and social gatherings across Istanbul—making it easier for both parents and children to build lasting friendships.
